name: Common hedge set by the acceleration of market funding (change, not level), spot basket always held
mechanism: The equal-weighted spot basket (fixed spot_budget, equal weights, drifting between two rebalances) is always held. The hedge is common to all listed pairs (spot and perp) and set by the CHANGE in market funding, not by its level. Each day, F_short is the 5-day average of the annualized funding rate averaged over eligible pairs (sum of the settlements actually received, scaled to the annualized rate by the actual duration covered), and F_long the average of the same values over long_window days. The acceleration is a = F_short - F_long. We make it unitless by dividing by the standard deviation of F_short over the previous 2 x long_window days: z = a / sigma. The hedged share is h = h_low + (1 - h_low) x clip((z + 2)/4, 0, 1), the same for all pairs. A high z means that demand for long leverage is growing fast: funding rises, so the short is paid more, and the risk of abrupt deleveraging increases with the speed of leverage accumulation (Brunnermeier and Pedersen: liquidity spirals arise when funding becomes tight after a buildup of positions). A low z (leverage unwinding or stable): little leverage to liquidate, we uncover. Since z is centered on its own recent history, the average hedge is about (1 + h_low)/2 if z is roughly symmetric, whatever the market phase. Difference from p-levier-niveau: here the signal is the derivative of leverage and not its level, so it is not a monotone function of the carry received; a high but stable funding leaves h in the middle. Difference from c-carry-regime and r-fonds-foule (discarded): no extreme threshold, no exit from the basket, no basis filter; a single continuous variable. The change in funding as an announcement of the coming premium is not a premium convergence signal (h-reversion-prime). Dead band on the perp leg. Shape guard (added by the auditor, mechanism unchanged): the perp weight sent for each pair is min(h x spot weight, spot weight), computed as a WEIGHT and not as perp quantity x perp price / V (a positive perp premium would otherwise push it above the spot long at h = 1: WEIGHT_SHAPE). Execution details (auditor's arbitration after adversarial review, source of return and mechanism unchanged): (1) CHAINED market funding. For each pair i and each day t, f_i,t is the annualized rate of the day (sum of settlements received that day, scaled to the year by the actual duration covered); absent if there is no settlement. d_t = average, over only the pairs whose f is present on days t and t-1, of f_i,t - f_i,t-1. If no pair is present on both days, d_t = 0: the day adds no value and erases nothing. Chained level L_t = L_(t-1) + d_t, L = 0 on the first day. F_short = average of L over the last 5 days, F_long = average of L over long_window days, a = F_short - F_long, sigma = standard deviation of F_short over the previous 2 x long_window days. A pair that enters (late listing, nine perps on the same day) contributes to d_t only from the day after its first value, so it creates no level jump. (2) Relative dead band. effective_band = min(dead_band, (1 - h_low)/4): 0.10 for h_low <= 0.60, 0.0875 at 0.65, 0.04 at 0.84. h is adjusted only if |target h - held h| > effective_band, OR if the target is exactly 1 or h_low (extremes of the clip) and the held h differs from the target: h then reaches 1 or h_low, never 0.90 for lack of a band.

name: Volatility targeting executed through the perp leg: spot held permanently, per-pair hedge set on intraday realized volatility
mechanism: The spot long is held permanently on the pairs that have both a spot and a perp listed (equal weights, sum of spot weights S0 = 0.60 of capital, which leaves 0.40 of margin for the perp at full hedge: 0.60 + 0.5 x 0.60 = 0.90). Only the perp leg moves. For each pair j and each day, we estimate the annualized realized volatility sigma_j from the 1h bars: realized variance of the day = sum of the squares of the 24 1h returns (close to close, missing bar = zero return), averaged over the last L days, multiplied by 365, square root (intraday realized variance estimator, much more precise than a single daily return). Target net exposure of the pair, as a share of its spot long: e_j = min(e_max, sigma_target / sigma_j); target hedge h_j = 1 - e_j, hence target perp short = h_j x spot weight of the pair. This is the Moreira-Muir volatility targeting (exposure inversely proportional to recent volatility), but the exposure is set by selling perp and not spot: the spot is not touched, spot turnover is almost zero and the adjustment cost is that of the perp (0.10%), not 0.60%. Incidentally, the hedged share earns the funding. Economic mechanism: volatility is very persistent whereas the expected return does not rise proportionally; in crypto, volatility spikes accompany chained liquidations of leveraged longs (Schmeling-Schrimpf-Todorov: margin calls and liquidations are concentrated in declines). Reducing net exposure when realized variance rises removes the riskiest part of the return without giving up the spot or the carry. Execution and turnover (by the strategy, which does not see its portfolio): it keeps its own book in QUANTITIES (spot units and perp units per pair) and its own net asset value V, recomputed each day: V_t = V_{t-1} x (1 + sum of spot weights x spot return - sum of perp weights x perp return + sum of perp weights x funding of the day), the returns coming from the daily closes and the funding from day.funding; the small costs are ignored in this recomputation. The weights sent to the engine are quantity x price / V, so price drift does not generate spot turnover (the engine's convention rebalances the weight drift). The perp quantity of a pair is modified only if the actual hedge departs from the target by more than the band (0.05, as a share of the spot long); the spot quantity is modified only when a pair enters the universe (new spot+perp listing: it is funded by proportionally reducing the others to return to equal weights summing to S0) or if the computed capital tied up exceeds 0.97 (guard against WEIGHT_SHAPE; the corresponding spot turnover is rare). Shape guard (added by the auditor, mechanism unchanged): the perp weight sent for each pair is min(h x spot weight, spot weight), computed as a WEIGHT and not as perp quantity x perp price / V (a positive perp premium would otherwise push it above the spot long at h = 1: WEIGHT_SHAPE). Difference from the families already played: the lab's V1 targets volatility by selling the spot basket (spot turnover at 0.60%, no carry); r-carry of wave 1 hedged 100% without a risk measure; here the hedge is continuous, per pair, and carries part of the market.

name: Cushion portfolio insurance (CPPI) executed through the perp leg: rolling floor on the net asset value recomputed by the strategy
mechanism: The spot long is held permanently (equal weights on the pairs with spot and perp listed, sum S0 = 0.60). The basket is hedged by default; the unhedged share, i.e. the net market exposure, is allocated according to a CPPI rule in the Black-Perold sense, with a floor on the portfolio's net asset value. The strategy does not see its value: it recomputes it each day, V_t = V_{t-1} x (1 + sum of spot weights x spot return - sum of perp weights x perp return + sum of perp weights x funding of the day), from the daily closes, day.funding and its own past weights (the small costs are ignored), with V_0 = 1. Rolling floor: P_t = (1 - f) x max of V over the last W days (the W-day memory avoids the permanent lock-in of a CPPI with a rising floor which, once at the floor, can only climb back through the carry). Cushion C_t = max(0, V_t - P_t). Target net exposure (as a share of capital): N_t = min(e_max x S0, m x C_t); common hedge h_t = 1 - N_t / S0 applied to each pair (perp short = h_t x spot weight of the pair). When V is at its recent high, the cushion is about f x V and net exposure is maximal (capped); when V falls toward the floor, the cushion melts and the hedge rises up to 100% (pure carry). Why this holds the drawdown by construction: with multiplier m = 4 fixed, the loss of the net share on a basket jump g is N x g <= m x C x g; if g < 1/m = 25% in one day, the value stays above the floor, so the drawdown from the W-day high is bounded by f, plus the excess of the jump beyond 25% and the costs; the cap e_max limits this jump to e_max x S0 x g. With f <= 0.06 the targeted drawdown stays below 20% (C6), with a margin for the measurement on capital tied up (division by 0.6 to 0.9). The carry of the hedged share lifts V and rebuilds the cushion. Execution: the book is kept in quantities (price drift does not generate spot turnover); the perp quantity is modified only if the target h_t departs from the actual hedge by more than 0.10 (band). Spot: modified only when a new pair arrives (rebalance to equal weights summing to S0) or if the computed capital tied up exceeds 0.97. Shape guard (added by the auditor, mechanism unchanged): the perp weight sent for each pair is min(h x spot weight, spot weight), computed as a WEIGHT and not as perp quantity x perp price / V (a positive perp premium would otherwise push it above the spot long at h = 1: WEIGHT_SHAPE). Difference from the families already played: the signal is not a property of the market but the net asset value of the strategy itself (a drawdown brake, not a forecast); none of the previous sheets used partial hedging or an insurance rule.

name: Trend strength normalized by volatility: moving-average gap relative to noise, graded hedge per pair
mechanism: Same portfolio skeleton: spot long of fixed weight w = 0.6 / max(n_eligible, 4) per listed pair (spot and perp), not rebalanced every day (the strategy follows the drift of its spot weights and only adjusts a pair on entry or outside a band of plus or minus 50%). Perp short = h x spot weight, h = 1 - a x u. Signal: for each pair, simple average of the closes over L/4 days (fast) and over L days (slow); sigma = standard deviation of the daily log returns over L days; z = ln(fast / slow) / (sigma x sqrt(L)): the gap between averages relative to the noise expected over the horizon, unitless, i.e. the trend strength in the sense of Baltas and Kosowski (a continuous trend statistic rather than a sign). u = clip(0.5 + 0.5 x z / zs, 0, 1): neutral state at u = 0.5, clear uptrend at u = 1, clear downtrend at u = 0; zs is the saturation. With fewer than L days of history, u = 0. Mechanism: a strong trend relative to the pair's volatility is more likely to last than a weak trend drowned in noise; the normalization makes the hedge vary slowly when the market is agitated and quickly when it is calm (the signal does not reverse on high-volatility noise). Baltas and Kosowski show that more efficient trend detection significantly reduces turnover and therefore rebalancing costs. Regularity is what gives the advantage here: a graded hedge costs the least in perp leg. Difference from a simple return sign: continuous and normalized by volatility, with two horizons (at low zs the signal is almost binary). Fixed settings a priori: a = 0.35, fast/slow ratio 1/4, total weight 0.6, drift band 50%. Execution (specified by the auditor, mechanism unchanged): the strategy recomputes its net asset value V_t = V_{t-1} x (1 + sum of spot weights x spot return - sum of perp weights x perp return + sum of perp weights x funding of the day), costs ignored, to convert its quantities into weights; it brings the spot back to the 0.6 budget if the computed capital tied up exceeds tied_capital_guard (without this guard, a common 50% rise of the pairs, band reached everywhere, would give 0.9 + 0.5 x 0.9 > 1: WEIGHT_SHAPE). The perp weight sent for each pair is min(h x spot weight, spot weight), computed as a weight and not as perp quantity x perp price / V (a positive perp premium would otherwise push it above the spot long at h = 1).
